skill.name: captain-obvious
skill.description: Audit TypeScript and Python tests for assertions that cannot fail or check nothing, and guide test authoring with a contract and regression gate. Use when writing or changing tests to avoid low-value coverage, or cleaning redundant, tautological, duplicated, or AI-generated tests. Cleanup runs bundled deterministic scanners; authoring guidance needs no scan during red-green TDD.
skill.summary: Find redundant TypeScript and Python tests, review uncertain assertions, and guide behavior-focused test authoring.
skill.author: shmulc8

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives involving documentation, template literals, AST identifiers, or legitimate toolchain operations. Confirmed risks involve shadow-file overwrite and deletion, plus symlink-following report writes to documented predictable temporary paths. The fix guards also permit irreversible changes to untracked tests; no evidence found of credential exfiltration or prompt injection.

remediation.issue: The Python type pass truncates existing shadow-named files and deletes those paths during cleanup.
remediation.suggestion: Create shadow files exclusively with unique names, reject existing paths, and remove only files created by the current invocation.

remediation.issue: Report writers follow symlinks, while documented examples use predictable paths in a shared temporary directory.
remediation.suggestion: Use a private temporary directory or securely created unique report files; reject symlink destinations and avoid truncating existing files without confirmation.

remediation.issue: Both fix guards ignore untracked files even though discovery and rewriting include untracked tests.
remediation.suggestion: Verify that every rewrite target is tracked and unchanged, or create recoverable backups before editing untracked or ignored tests.

semantic_findings.title: Untracked Tests Bypass Recovery Safeguards
semantic_findings.description: Both Git guards use --untracked-files=no, but test discovery includes untracked files. --fix can overwrite those tests without backups or Git restoration.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both guards explicitly exclude untracked files, while discovery and fixers do not restrict edits to tracked targets. Neither fixer creates recovery backups.

content.user_title: Audit TypeScript and Python Test Quality
content.value_statement: Redundant assertions can inflate confidence without protecting observable behavior. Captain Obvious combines deterministic scanners with contextual review and a test-authoring contract checklist.
actual_capabilities: Detect constant assertions, local constant echoes, dead assertions, mock echoes, and duplicate test bodies in supported test styles.
Use TypeScript compiler information and optional mypy probes to identify assertions already implied by declared types.
Separate findings into proven and advisory levels, with explanations and deletion metadata.
Read lcov, Istanbul, or coverage.py reports to refine conditional assertion findings.
Generate removal plans and optionally edit findings marked safe through an explicit fix command.
Guide test authoring with contract questions and compare new syntactic findings against a Git baseline.
limitations: Pattern detection cannot establish complete test effectiveness or replace mutation testing and contract review.
TypeScript requires a resolvable TypeScript package; Python type checks require runnable mypy and may create temporary shadow files.
Scanning can execute repository toolchain code; Python shadow files and untracked fix targets have recovery risks.
Dynamic assertions and some parameterized TypeScript test forms are unsupported; coverage refinement requires coverage of test files.

use_cases.title: Review Generated Test Suites
use_cases.description: Find tautologies and mock echoes in generated tests, then review advisory findings against the production behavior.

use_cases.title: Maintain Shared Test Standards
use_cases.description: Use contract questions and documented detector categories to distinguish meaningful regression checks from redundant assertions during review.

use_cases.title: Compare Test Changes in CI
use_cases.description: Compare supported proven syntactic findings against a Git baseline without enabling fixes. Comparison errors return success with a diagnostic.

prompt_templates.title: Review One Python Test
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Python test using the authoring questions. Identify its observable contract and a plausible regression. Do not run commands or edit files.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: understand whether a test protects behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Report-Only Python Audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this trusted Python repository with --no-types and without --fix. Use stdout instead of a report file. Summarize findings without deleting tests.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: inspect syntactic findings without shadow-file creation.

prompt_templates.title: Review Coverage-Based Findings
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this trusted TypeScript project using its existing coverage report. Separate proven and advisory findings. Propose advisory changes for approval; do not edit files.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: inspect conditional assertions using existing execution data.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Baseline Quality Check
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the --check workflow for this trusted repository against [base]. Explain fail-open behavior and excluded categories. Propose a report-only CI command for approval.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert: evaluate a baseline comparison before CI integration.

output_examples.input: Review a Python test that assigns a local value of five and immediately checks that it equals five.
output: Reason: the assertion repeats the test arrangement and does not inspect production behavior.
Next step: identify the intended contract before replacing or removing the test.

output_examples.input: Review a TypeScript promise rejection assertion that is not awaited.
output: Reason: failure behavior depends on the test runner, and the assertion is not awaited.
Proposal: await the assertion, then run the focused test after approval.

output_examples.input: Review a conditional assertion when coverage shows that its line never executed.
output: Finding: conditional assertion promoted to proven by coverage.
Reason: the supplied coverage report records zero executions for the assertion line.
Proposal: investigate the guard and preserve the intended contract. Do not automatically delete this report-only finding.

best_practices: Scan only trusted repositories, start without fixes, and avoid predictable shared temporary report paths.
Back up untracked tests and existing shadow-named files before scanning or fixing; Python --no-types avoids shadow-file creation.
Review each proposed deletion against its contract, obtain approval for advisory edits, and run type checks and tests afterward.
anti_patterns: Treating a clean scanner report as proof that every test can detect meaningful regressions.
Deleting advisory findings or weakening security contract tests solely because their assertions look repetitive.
Using --force, trusting Git cleanliness for untracked files, or running repository toolchains without reviewing their trust boundary.

faq.question: Which languages and test styles are supported?
faq.answer: The bundled scanners target TypeScript and JavaScript Jest-style or Vitest-style tests, plus Python pytest and unittest patterns.

faq.question: Does scanning execute my tests?
faq.answer: The scanners parse tests rather than run the test suite. They can load repository TypeScript code or execute mypy plugins and environment commands.

faq.question: Can I scan without modifying Python files?
faq.answer: Use --no-types without --fix or a file output option. Single-file Python mode also parses source without mypy shadow files.

faq.question: Are all findings automatically deleted?
faq.answer: No. Explicit --fix targets findings marked safe. Advisory and report-only findings require review, and advisory edits require user approval.

faq.question: What does coverage input add?
faq.answer: Coverage can confirm that a conditional assertion never executed or suppress a finding when it did. The report must include test-file lines.

faq.question: Can the baseline check enforce every finding?
faq.answer: No. It compares newly introduced proven syntactic findings. Type-dependent and coverage-dependent categories are excluded, and comparison failures return success with diagnostics.
